summary: The note describes outdoor yoga and fitness classes held in Central Park, led by yogi Samantha Greene and trainer Eric Thompson since September 1, 2023. Each Saturday session pairs a 45-minute Vinyasa-based yoga class with high-intensity interval training, and fosters community, mental well-being, and inclusivity. The classes are credited with encouraging healthier habits and with plans for expansion into more exercise types and wellness workshops.
one_line: Samantha Greene and Eric Thompson lead popular Saturday-morning outdoor yoga and interval training classes in Central Park, building community and healthier habits.
key_facts: The outdoor yoga and fitness classes have run since September 1, 2023.
The initiative is led by yogi Samantha Greene and fitness guru Eric Thompson.
Samantha Greene has 10 years of experience in Hatha yoga.
Eric Thompson is a decade-long personal trainer specializing in high-intensity interval training.
Classes take place every Saturday morning at the break of dawn in Central Park and began as small gatherings among friends.
Each class starts with a 45-minute yoga session led by Samantha, with eco-friendly yoga mats provided to participants.
The yoga is rooted in the Vinyasa tradition, a dynamic flow emphasizing breath control and awareness.

Eric's interval training uses open fields, park benches for step-ups and push-ups, and body-weight resistance; he says, "With the park as our playground, we've got all we need for a full-body workout."
Regular attendee Melissa Jones said she used to struggle with motivation but found a community through the classes.
Attendees report significant improvements in mood, stress levels, and overall mental well-being.
Instructors offer exercise modifications so the classes suit all ages and fitness levels, from young adults to the elderly, including parents with children.
The community has observed a surge in cycling to work, walking during lunch breaks, and impromptu outdoor fitness meet-ups.
Local authorities have taken note of the trend, ensuring the maintenance and safety of parks.
Future plans include more diverse forms of exercise and wellness workshops.
